extracted.intended_audience: current or prospective Public Information Officers (PIOs) in government or quasi-government public safety / emergency services organizations seeking CPSE PIO qualification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility standards for becoming a CPSE Public Information Officer (PIO) within governmental or quasi‑governmental public safety and emergency services organizations, including professional skills expectations and a 150‑point qualification system based on education and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing robust relationships with the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing robust relationships with the media is paramount for PIOs, ensuring accurate and timely information dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes proactive media engagement and maintaining media contacts so that information released is both accurate and timely; presented as a core PIO duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shaping narratives, managing sensitive data, and delivering clear, reassuring messages (crisis/message management)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO plays a pivotal role in shaping narratives, managing sensitive data, and delivering clear, reassuring messages, especially during crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs must be able to control message framing and handle sensitive information appropriately to reassure the public in high‑stress situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailoring messages to diverse audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastering the art of tailoring messages to diverse audiences is imperative, fostering connections between different communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should be adapted to reach different demographic, cultural, and stakeholder groups effectively; audience‑specific messaging is highlighted as essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigating the digital landscape and utilizing social media
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs adeptly navigate the digital landscape, utilizing social media platforms to extend their reach and engage effectively with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active, strategic use of social media is expected to broaden reach and engagement; digital channels are part of core competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community outreach and preparedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Community outreach and preparedness are integral components of a PIO’s role within governmental or quasi‑governmental entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Building and nurturing relationships within the community and educating the public on safety measures enhances public safety and strengthens agency‑community connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upholding honesty, transparency, and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Upholding honesty, transparency, and accuracy is paramount for maintaining public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In challenging circumstances the community relies on the PIO and the agency for truthful and reliable information; maintaining these principles is presented as crucial to credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment/affiliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for PIO, a person must be employed full or part‑time, contracted with, or volunteer for a government agency, public safety agency, emergency services organization, or a privately owned industry that supports government or serves in emergency support functions (ESF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to individuals who have an official relationship with an appropriate governmental/public safety/emergency support organization; volunteers and contractors are included if they serve within those functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 150‑point qualification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 150 points, which can be earned through education and [experience].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must accumulate a total of 150 points to qualify; points are awarded across education and experience categories (text indicates education and experience are the primary sources of points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Education points range
rubrics_metrics.description: Points for education range from 25 to 150 and can include an Academic Certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational credentials contribute a variable number of points (minimum 25 up to the full 150); academic certificates are explicitly listed as acceptable education evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience points range
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience points range from 5 to 60 and may be influenced by the length of time in the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical time served in PIO or related roles contributes points toward the 150‑point requirement; longer tenure yields more experience points within the stated range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational chart requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing an organizational chart is required to confirm their position within the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit an org chart as documentary proof of their official role/placement in the department to validate eligibility.
